```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(hydroloom)
eval <- (Sys.getenv("BUILD_VIGNETTES") == "TRUE") &
  requireNamespace("hydrogeofetch", quietly = TRUE) &
  requireNamespace("lwgeom", quietly = TRUE)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 6,
  fig.height = 6,
  fig.align = "center",
  eval = eval
)

library(sf)

oldoption <- options(scipen = 9999)
```

This article crosswalks a point from one network to another. The point is
indexed to a flowline (an `id` and a measure along it), recorded as a signed
distance from the nearest confluence, and placed on the second network. The
same point as a measure along the whole mainstem (an `aggregate_id_measure`)
is then recorded as a distance from the same confluence on the second network,
and the two positions compared. Last, `get_subpath()` cuts the stretch
between two positions, once for one flowline of the first network on the
second and once across a confluence, where the stretch spans two mainstems.

The NHDPlusV2 flowlines and the mainstem URI lookup ship with hydroloom. The
3DHP sample comes from hydrogeofetch. This article is website-only and does
not run on CRAN.

![Map of the New Hope sample flowlines with the New Hope River, Northeast Creek, and Morgan Creek mainstems highlighted, the three mainstems as drawn by 3DHP in orange over grey 3DHP waterbody polygons, a triangle at the Northeast Creek confluence, and a dot at the referenced point](mainstem_referencing_setting.png)

The setting: three identified mainstems in the New Hope sample. The triangle
is the confluence used as the hydro location, where Northeast Creek enters the
New Hope River, and the dot is the point whose position is recorded as a
distance from it. The orange lines are the same three mainstems as 3DHP draws
them, over 3DHP waterbodies in grey.

# Confluence referenced Hydrologic locations: concepts 

A streamgage, a sample site, or an intake is at the outlet of a specific
drainage area. That area grows a little at a time with local drainage
between confluences and jumps by a whole tributary basin at each one. A
position recorded a few hundred meters off along the river, but on the correct
side of a confluence, drains nearly the same area as the true position. A
position a few meters off but across a confluence does not.

A position indexed to a flowline is that flowline's `id` and a measure along
it. A reachcode and measure (an NHD event) is instead a measure along a
reachcode aggregate flowpath; `rescale_measures()` converts it to a flowline
measure the same way the HydroAdd3D address is converted below, though that
path is not demonstrated here. The `id` belongs to a specific network: the NHDPlusV2
`COMID`, the NHDPlusHR `nhdplusid`, the 3DHP `id3dhp`. It does not carry to
another network, and the 3DHP `id3dhp` is not stable between 3DHP releases.

In contrast, a mainstem URI is durable, and so is a confluence: the place one
identified mainstem enters another is present on any network that carries both
mainstems. A position recorded as a signed distance along a mainstem from one
of its confluences can be placed on any such network, but only approximately,
because each network has unique flowline geometry and its own placement of the
confluence, so the same distance will land at different points on the ground.
What transfers intact is whether the position is upstream or downstream of the
confluence.

```{r mainstems}
library(hydroloom)
library(sf)

ne <- "https://geoconnex.us/ref/mainstems/2408627"  # Northeast Creek
mc <- "https://geoconnex.us/ref/mainstems/2408909"  # Morgan Creek
nh <- "https://geoconnex.us/ref/mainstems/2408056"  # New Hope River
```

# The two networks

The first network, `v2`, is a set of flowlines joined to a lookup of mainstem
URIs, with the URI as `aggregate_id`. A recipe shipped with hydroloom does the
join and casts the flowlines to `LINESTRING` so `get_subpath()` can cut them.

```{r v2}
source(system.file("extdata", "new_hope_mainstems.R", package = "hydroloom"))

v2 <- add_toids(hy(new_hope_mainstems))
```

The second network, `net_3dhp`, carries mainstem URIs natively. `toid` comes from
matching `dnhydrosequence` to `hydrosequence`, which also serves as
`topo_sort`.

```{r threedhp}
source(system.file("extdata", "new_hope_3dhp.R", package = "hydrogeofetch"))

raw_3dhp <- sf::read_sf(sample_new_hope_3dhp)

m <- match(raw_3dhp$dnhydrosequence, raw_3dhp$hydrosequence)
raw_3dhp$toid <- raw_3dhp$id3dhp[m]
raw_3dhp$toid[is.na(raw_3dhp$toid)] <- ""

raw_3dhp <- sf::st_zm(raw_3dhp)
raw_3dhp <- dplyr::transmute(raw_3dhp,
  id = id3dhp, toid = toid, aggregate_id = mainstemid,
  topo_sort = hydrosequence, length_km = lengthkm, divergence = divergence)

net_3dhp <- hy(raw_3dhp)
```

`get_confluences()` finds every place one identified mainstem enters another.
Each confluence is a hydro location on the receiving mainstem, identified by
the tributary's `aggregate_id` and placed at the upstream end of the first
receiving flowline below the tributary.

```{r confluences}
v2conf <- get_confluences(v2)
conf_3dhp <- get_confluences(net_3dhp)

ne_v2 <- v2conf[v2conf$hydro_location_id == ne, ]
ne_3dhp <- conf_3dhp[conf_3dhp$hydro_location_id == ne, ]

ne_v2
ne_3dhp
```

Both networks place the tributary's confluence (`ne`) on the receiving mainstem
(`nh`). The flowline that holds it differs, as the two `id` columns show. The
confluence is durable, the flowline is not.

# A point on the receiving mainstem

Take a point near the confluence and index it to the receiving mainstem on the
first network, constraining the search with `aggregate_ids` and refining the
measure with `precision` (see [resolving
ambiguity](https://doi-usgs.github.io/hydroloom/articles/indexing.html#resolving-ambiguity)
in the indexing article).

```{r index}
point <- sf::st_centroid(sf::st_geometry(v2[v2$id == ne_v2$id, ]))
point_sf <- sf::st_sf(geometry = point)

idx <- index_points_to_lines(v2, point_sf, aggregate_ids = nh, precision = 10)
idx
```

`add_hydro_location_distance()` records that position as a signed distance
from the nearest hydro location. Passing the one confluence as the only hydro
location measures from it in particular. The sign is negative
because the point sits downstream of the confluence.

```{r distance}
rec <- add_hydro_location_distance(
  data.frame(id = idx$id, id_measure = idx$id_measure), ne_v2, v2)
rec
```

# Placing the record on the second network

The record is a mainstem, a confluence, and a signed distance.
`index_hydro_location_distance()` places it on the second network without
reference to the flowline it was recorded on: it finds the confluence on the
second network's aggregate flowpath axis, adds the distance, and maps the
result to a flowline and measure there.

```{r resolve}
record <- data.frame(aggregate_id = rec$aggregate_id,
  hydro_location_id = rec$hydro_location_id, distance_km = rec$distance_km)

onto3 <- index_hydro_location_distance(record, ne_3dhp, net_3dhp)
onto3
```

`status` is `placed`: the distance fell within the mainstem's flowlines in
`net_3dhp`. `past_end` would mean it ran past the downstream or upstream end of
those flowlines, with `past_end_km` giving how far.

The point and the flowline that holds it on each network, in the same window
as the figure at the top of the article:

```{r map_setup}
half <- 5200
ctr <- c(1515500, 1557000)
view <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = ctr[1] - half, ymin = ctr[2] - half,
  xmax = ctr[1] + half, ymax = ctr[2] + half), crs = sf::st_crs(v2)))

# the three mainstems as the second network draws them
ms_3dhp <- sf::st_transform(
  net_3dhp[!is.na(net_3dhp$aggregate_id) &
    net_3dhp$aggregate_id %in% c(nh, ne, mc), ], sf::st_crs(v2))

# waterbodies of the second network in the window, fetched from the service
wb <- hydrogeofetch::get_3dhp(AOI = sf::st_transform(view, 4326),
  type = "waterbody")
wb <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_zm(wb), sf::st_crs(v2))
```

```{r map}
nh_v2 <- v2[!is.na(v2$aggregate_id) & v2$aggregate_id == nh, ]
nh_3dhp <- sf::st_transform(
  net_3dhp[!is.na(net_3dhp$aggregate_id) & net_3dhp$aggregate_id == nh, ], sf::st_crs(v2))

v2_line <- nh_v2[nh_v2$id == idx$id, ]
line_3dhp <- nh_3dhp[nh_3dhp$id == onto3$id, ]

plot(view, border = NA, reset = FALSE)
plot(sf::st_geometry(v2), add = TRUE, col = "grey80", lwd = 0.7)
plot(sf::st_geometry(ms_3dhp), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 1)
plot(sf::st_geometry(nh_v2), add = TRUE, col = "lightblue", lwd = 2)
plot(sf::st_geometry(v2_line), add = TRUE, col = "darkblue", lwd = 3)
plot(sf::st_geometry(line_3dhp), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 3)
plot(sf::st_geometry(point_sf), add = TRUE, pch = 16, col = "black")
```

The point (black) sits on the receiving mainstem. The flowline it was indexed
to on the first network (dark blue) and the flowline the record was placed on
in the second (heavy red, over the second network's mainstems in thin red)
cover the same stretch of river with different lines.

The placed position is approximate. The second network draws the mainstem with
its own line and puts the confluence at its own spot on it, so 0.75 km below
that spot is not the same point on the ground as 0.75 km below the confluence
on the first network. What the record preserves is that the position is
downstream of the confluence.

# From a mainstem measure

A position can also be given as a measure along a whole mainstem: a mainstem
URI and a measure `m`, 0 at the mainstem's downstream end and 100 at its head.
HydroAdd3D (the USGS hydrographic addressing service for 3DHP) returns
locations in this form. The measure moves whenever the mainstem's flowlines
are edited, extended, or re-delineated, since a percent of the length changes
with the length. A
distance from a confluence holds as long as both mainstems exist.

`hydrogeofetch::get_3dhp_index()` calls the service; its
[example](https://doi-usgs.github.io/hydrogeofetch/reference/get_3dhp_index.html)
shows the full response. The address below is written in that shape for the
point used above, with `m` set to the value hydroloom gets indexing the same
point to the second network.

```{r address}
address <- data.frame(source_id = "1", mainstemid = nh, m = 29.53)
```

`m` is an `aggregate_id_measure` in hydroloom terms. The flowlines of `net_3dhp`
do not carry from and to measures along the mainstem, so `add_measures()`
computes them from geometry, projected first so lengths are in meters. It
needs the whole mainstem, which the sample carries.

```{r address-measures}
nh_3dhp_m <- net_3dhp[!is.na(net_3dhp$aggregate_id) & net_3dhp$aggregate_id == nh, ]
nh_3dhp_m <- add_measures(sf::st_transform(nh_3dhp_m, 5070))
```

The flowline whose measure interval holds `m` carries the address, and
`rescale_measures()` converts the mainstem measure to a measure along that
flowline. From there the position is like any other, and
`add_hydro_location_distance()` records it as kilometers from the confluence.

```{r address-distance}
fl <- nh_3dhp_m[nh_3dhp_m$aggregate_id_from_measure <= address$m &
  nh_3dhp_m$aggregate_id_to_measure > address$m, ]

pos <- data.frame(id = fl$id,
  id_measure = rescale_measures(address$m, fl$aggregate_id_from_measure,
    fl$aggregate_id_to_measure))

from_address <- add_hydro_location_distance(pos, ne_3dhp, net_3dhp)
from_address
```

The map shows both positions as points on the second network, along with the
input point and its snap onto that network's line. `st_line_sample()` takes a
fraction from the first vertex, which is the upstream end, so the fraction is
`1 - id_measure / 100`.

```{r address-map}
on_line <- function(ids, measures) {
  lines <- nh_3dhp_m[match(ids, nh_3dhp_m$id), ]
  sf::st_cast(sf::st_line_sample(lines, sample = 1 - measures / 100), "POINT")
}

p_record <- on_line(onto3$id, onto3$id_measure)
p_address <- on_line(pos$id, pos$id_measure)

point_3d <- sf::st_transform(point_sf, 5070)
snap <- sf::st_nearest_points(point_3d, nh_3dhp_m[nh_3dhp_m$id == pos$id, ])

conf_3d <- sf::st_transform(net_3dhp[net_3dhp$id == ne_3dhp$id, ], 5070)
p_conf <- sf::st_cast(sf::st_line_sample(conf_3d, sample = 0), "POINT")

view <- sf::st_buffer(sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(p_record, p_address, p_conf))), 300)

all_3d <- sf::st_transform(net_3dhp, 5070)
v2_3d <- sf::st_transform(nh_v2, 5070)

plot(view, border = NA, reset = FALSE)
plot(sf::st_geometry(sf::st_transform(wb, 5070)), add = TRUE, col = "grey90",
  border = NA)
plot(sf::st_geometry(all_3d), add = TRUE, col = "grey70", lwd = 1)
plot(sf::st_geometry(v2_3d), add = TRUE, col = "lightblue", lwd = 3)
plot(sf::st_geometry(nh_3dhp_m), add = TRUE, col = "grey30", lwd = 2)
plot(sf::st_geometry(nh_3dhp_m[nh_3dhp_m$id == pos$id, ]), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 3)
plot(snap, add = TRUE, lty = 2)
plot(sf::st_geometry(point_3d), add = TRUE, pch = 16, col = "black", cex = 1.2)
plot(p_conf, add = TRUE, pch = 17, col = "darkgreen", cex = 1.5)
plot(p_record, add = TRUE, pch = 21, bg = "darkblue", cex = 1.5)
plot(p_address, add = TRUE, pch = 21, bg = "orange", cex = 1.5)

legend("topleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.8,
  legend = c("NHDPlusV2 New Hope River", "3DHP New Hope River",
    "3DHP flowline 2VMGA", "other 3DHP flowlines", "input point",
    "snap onto 3DHP", "Northeast Creek confluence",
    "record transferred from NHDPlusV2", "HydroAdd3D address",
    "3DHP waterbody"),
  col = c("lightblue", "grey30", "red", "grey70", "black", "black",
    "darkgreen", "black", "black", "grey70"),
  lwd = c(3, 2, 3, 1, NA, 1, NA, NA, NA, NA),
  lty = c(1, 1, 1, 1, NA, 2, NA, NA, NA, NA),
  pch = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, 16, NA, 17, 21, 21, 22),
  pt.bg = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, "darkblue", "orange", "grey90"),
  pt.cex = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, 1, NA, 1, 1, 1, 1.8))
```

The address (orange) lands on the same flowline as the record transferred from
the first network (dark blue), about 0.2 km further downstream of the
confluence. The record says 0.75 km below the confluence, measured along the
first network's lines from its placement of the confluence. On the second
network that 0.75 km is laid out along different lines from a confluence
placed somewhere else. The address instead starts from where the point snaps
onto the second network's line, about 140 m across from it.

The 0.2 km is the approximation in absolute terms: the confluence sits at a
different spot on each network, and the kilometers are laid out from wherever
each network puts it. The side of the confluence agrees. On both networks the
point is downstream of the confluence, so it sees the tributary's drainage
either way. The 0.2 km between the two positions moves the point along the
mainstem with no tributary entering between them, which changes its upstream
area only by the local drainage along that stretch. Where geometric position
has to be exact on the target network, index the original point (or a
mainstem measure) on that network rather than transferring the distance.

# One flowline's subpath on the second network

A single flowline of the first network maps to a span of flowlines on the
second. Index both of its ends to the second network with `aggregate_ids`,
then `get_subpath()` returns the ordered pieces between them. An end can sit a
few hundred meters from the second network's line, so the search radius is
raised to 500 m; `aggregate_ids` keeps the wider radius from pulling an end
onto a tributary (see [resolving
ambiguity](https://doi-usgs.github.io/hydroloom/articles/indexing.html#resolving-ambiguity)).

```{r subpath}
src <- v2[v2$id == idx$id, ]

e_from <- sf::st_transform(get_node(src, "end"), sf::st_crs(net_3dhp))
e_to <- sf::st_transform(get_node(src, "start"), sf::st_crs(net_3dhp))

rad <- units::set_units(500, "m")
i_from <- index_points_to_lines(net_3dhp, e_from, aggregate_ids = nh, search_radius = rad)
i_to <- index_points_to_lines(net_3dhp, e_to, aggregate_ids = nh, search_radius = rad)

piece <- get_subpath(
  data.frame(id = i_from$id, id_measure = i_from$id_measure),
  data.frame(id = i_to$id, id_measure = i_to$id_measure), net_3dhp)

sf::st_drop_geometry(piece)
```

`segment_order` runs from 1 at the downstream end upward; `id_from_measure` and
`id_to_measure` cut the end pieces; `length_km` is the piece length. Because
`net_3dhp` is `sf` and lwgeom is installed, each piece also carries its cut
geometry.

The source flowline, its two ends snapped onto the second network, and the
pieces cut between them:

```{r subpath-map}
src_3d <- sf::st_transform(src, 5070)
piece_3d <- sf::st_transform(piece, 5070)
end_from <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_geometry(e_from), 5070)
end_to <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_geometry(e_to), 5070)

snap_from <- sf::st_nearest_points(end_from, nh_3dhp_m[nh_3dhp_m$id == i_from$id, ])
snap_to <- sf::st_nearest_points(end_to, nh_3dhp_m[nh_3dhp_m$id == i_to$id, ])

view <- sf::st_buffer(sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(
  c(sf::st_geometry(src_3d), sf::st_geometry(piece_3d)))), 300)

plot(view, border = NA, reset = FALSE)
plot(sf::st_geometry(sf::st_transform(wb, 5070)), add = TRUE, col = "grey90",
  border = NA)
plot(sf::st_geometry(all_3d), add = TRUE, col = "grey70", lwd = 1)
plot(sf::st_geometry(v2_3d), add = TRUE, col = "lightblue", lwd = 3)
plot(sf::st_geometry(src_3d), add = TRUE, col = "darkblue", lwd = 3)
plot(sf::st_geometry(nh_3dhp_m), add = TRUE, col = "grey30", lwd = 2)
plot(sf::st_geometry(piece_3d), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 3)
plot(snap_from, add = TRUE, lty = 2)
plot(snap_to, add = TRUE, lty = 2)
plot(c(end_from, end_to), add = TRUE, pch = 16, col = "black", cex = 1.2)

legend("topleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.8,
  legend = c("NHDPlusV2 New Hope River", "NHDPlusV2 source flowline",
    "3DHP New Hope River", "subpath pieces", "other 3DHP flowlines",
    "source flowline ends", "snap onto 3DHP", "3DHP waterbody"),
  col = c("lightblue", "darkblue", "grey30", "red", "grey70", "black",
    "black", "grey70"),
  lwd = c(3, 3, 2, 3, 1, NA, 1, NA),
  lty = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, NA, 2, NA),
  pch = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, 16, NA, 22),
  pt.bg = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, "grey90"),
  pt.cex = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, 1, NA, 1.8))
```

# A stretch across a confluence

A stretch from a second tributary (`mc`) down onto the receiving mainstem spans
two mainstems. `get_subpath()` takes two positions on one aggregate flowpath,
so the stretch is two calls split at that tributary's confluence, which lies on
both mainstems.

```{r stretch}
mc_v2 <- v2conf[v2conf$hydro_location_id == mc, ]

on_mc <- v2[!is.na(v2$aggregate_id) & v2$aggregate_id == mc, ]
on_nh <- v2[!is.na(v2$aggregate_id) & v2$aggregate_id == nh, ]

# Morgan Creek, from an upstream point down to its mouth
up_mc <- data.frame(id = on_mc$id[which.max(on_mc$topo_sort)], id_measure = 100)
mouth_mc <- data.frame(id = on_mc$id[which.min(on_mc$topo_sort)], id_measure = 0)
seg_mc <- get_subpath(up_mc, mouth_mc, v2)

# New Hope River, from the confluence downstream
conf_nh <- data.frame(id = mc_v2$id, id_measure = 100)
down_nh <- data.frame(id = on_nh$id[which.min(on_nh$topo_sort)], id_measure = 0)
seg_nh <- get_subpath(conf_nh, down_nh, v2)

head(sf::st_drop_geometry(seg_mc))
head(sf::st_drop_geometry(seg_nh))
```

`reversed` is `TRUE` because each `from` was given upstream of its `to`; the
pieces still come back downstream to upstream. The two sets meet at the
confluence. To hold the whole stretch as one table, concatenate them in flow
order, the tributary pieces above the receiving mainstem pieces.

```{r reset, include = FALSE}
options(oldoption)
```
